result_text:
Suppliers now carry payment terms in days. A new supplier defaults to 30 days, and the terms can be changed later through `updateSupplier`. The full offline suite passes: 176 suites, no failures.

What changed:

- **`model/Supplier.java`**: new `paymentTermsDays` component. The existing 5-argument constructor is kept and defaults to 30, so the demo data and existing tests compile unchanged.
- **`resources/schema.sql`**: `payment_terms_days INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 30 CHECK (payment_terms_days >= 0)` on `supplier`.
- **`DataStorePart01.java`**: create and update write the terms. The three listings (all by name, by country, by minimum rating) read them.
- **`DataStorePart09.java`**: `findSupplierById` reads them. The performance, spending, and category-single-supplier queries also select them, so every `Supplier` built anywhere carries the real value.
- **`DataStorePart02.java`** and **`DataStorePart03.java`**: the purchase-suggestion and purchased-quantity queries also select the column, for the same reason.
- **`SupplierTest.java`**: new test covering the default of 30, a 45-day supplier renegotiated to 14, and 14 days shown in every listing and lookup.

I did not add a payment-terms parameter to the service layer, since the task only asked for the data store to hold and show the value. Say if you want a service or UI entry point as well. I also did not touch the demo data, so demo suppliers still show 30 days.
